findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1216-1221 (writeCodexProcessEvent) excludes ONLY entry.command==="quorum_submit" from the generic post-handler codex_cli process-event append, with a comment stating this is because quorum_submit "owns one exact immutable process-events transaction inside its handler" and a generic append "would make that canonical commit dirty again". quorum_prune (packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:20-22,338-365) commits process-events.jsonl through the IDENTICAL captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction/commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction machinery and its own header comment explicitly claims parity ("committed through the SAME lifecycle-metadata transaction machinery quorum_submit uses so the pre-dirty refusal, exact-content verification, and rollback all hold") — a claim also repeated in command-policy.ts:480 and process-fact-levels.ts:209, both touched by this diff. cli-engine.ts was NOT updated to add the matching exclusion for quorum_prune. Live repro (built dist, temp git fixture, LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex): `lattice quorum_prune --apply` succeeds and commits cleanly (HEAD advances, applied:true), but immediately after, `git status --porcelain` shows `M .lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl` — the exact file quorum_prune just atomically committed is re-dirtied by the unguarded generic codex_cli append, which is the precise poisoning mode the sibling comment for quorum_submit exists to prevent. This leftover dirty state then makes quorum_prune/quorum_submit pre-dirty-refuse on the very next call for reasons unrelated to genuine story changes. No test in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts exercises `quorum_prune --apply` through the real CLI (runFixtureCli, which sets LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex) with a post-command git-status-clean assertion (unlike the existing quorum_submit CLI test at line ~939 which does assert `git status --porcelain=v1===`), so this gap is untested. WHY: the diff repeatedly promises quorum_prune has transactional parity with quorum_submit including pre-dirty-refusal integrity, but the one cross-file wiring point that actually protects that guarantee under Codex-driven sessions was left half-registered.
findings.resolvedReason: cli-engine.ts now excludes quorum_prune from the generic codex_cli process-event append, kept as its own literal statement because verify-process-fact-contract.mjs pins the quorum_submit line. New smoke check runs quorum_prune --apply through the built CLI under LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex and asserts git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all is empty. RED-verified: patching the exclusion out of the built dist made the check fail with exactly 'M .lattice/story/actives/B-quorum-smoke/process-events.jsonl'. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: handlers/quorum-prune.ts:125-135 writeUniqueBackup() writes the pre-prune backup directly into the git-tracked story dir (.lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>) and NEVER stages/commits/gitignores it (no matching *.bak-* gitignore pattern; the *.bak pattern at .gitignore does not match the .bak-<timestamp> suffix). Verified live: after `quorum_prune {apply:true}` succeeds, `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` in the story dir shows `?? .../process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>` (repro output captured). Both assertCleanPruneBaseline (quorum-prune.ts:112-123, called at :336) and assertCleanQuorumBaseline (quorum-submit.ts:219-228, called at :529) do a raw whole-tree `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` with zero exemption for this file, so the very first legitimate follow-up action after a successful recovery -- another quorum_prune apply, OR a genuinely-new quorum_submit once the story-owned files change -- throws "worktree/index must be clean"/"nothing to prune" refusals caused entirely by the tool's own leftover backup, not by real user dirt. The same unexempted --untracked-files=all pattern is reused broadly (validation-executor.ts:202, done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:362, dirty-worktree-gate.ts:42, recover-evidence.ts:68, cross-host-review.ts:81), so a leftover backup can also block TEST/DONE-adjacent gates. This directly undermines the story's stated goal ("the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level" / official low-friction recovery) since the operator must now manually discover and clean up (commit, delete, or gitignore) the tool's own artifact before doing anything else in the story. None of the 12 quorum_prune smoke checks catch this: the one test that runs quorum_prune apply twice ("never overwrites a previous run backup") masks it by doing its own `git add -A; git commit` between the two applies, which incidentally absorbs the first backup file into a commit -- a step a real operator/recovery workflow would not necessarily perform.
findings.resolvedReason: writeUniqueBackup now names the backup process-events.jsonl.<stamp>.bak with the collision counter BEFORE the extension, so every candidate genuinely matches the existing .gitignore *.bak rule. Neither assertCleanPruneBaseline nor assertCleanQuorumBaseline was weakened and no bespoke exemption was added. New smoke check runs apply twice in a row with NO intervening git command and the second apply succeeds. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:519-526 vs packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1665-1669: intent requires the refusal message to be verified as naming standing runIds, materialDigest of the standing verdicts, and pointing at review_escalation_status. The production message does contain all of that, but the ONLY assertion against it anywhere in the smoke suite is assert.match(..., /quorum_submit refuses: .*drift-accept/i, ...) at line 1667 (and /drift-accept/i at 1711/1714) -- neither checks for runIds, materialDigest values, or the literal string review_escalation_status. The verificationEvidence note for CHK-002:edge:2 ("Drift-branch message content asserted via regex; message names standing runIds, older material(s), current storyFilesHash, poisoning consequence, and points at review_escalation_status") overstates what the bound regex actually verifies -- it is true of the production code, not of the test assertion.
findings.resolvedReason: The drift-accept refusal check now asserts the message contains all three standing runIds, the older materialDigest, the current storyFilesHash, and the literal review_escalation_status pointer, instead of only matching /drift-accept/. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-003:happy:2 evidence cites an unbound command, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2098-2113: the checklist scope.allowedModify explicitly includes packages/main/src/core/config.ts (DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS wiring), and config.ts:362 does add quorum_prune to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS. But the bound checks own comment (~2106-2109) says exercising that wiring is "outside this storys scope contract" and is not tested there (only catalog+policy resolution and non-unknown-command dispatch are asserted). The verificationEvidence note for CHK-003:happy:2 instead claims coverage via "scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs passes with the new fact row and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS entry" -- but that script is a different, separate command from the one this evidence row is bound to (node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js), and no verificationEvidence row records that script having been run at this headHash/materialHash. The claimed "wiring verification across all 5 integration points" is therefore not actually demonstrated by evidence bound to this storys own smoke command for the config.ts integration point.
findings.resolvedReason: The CLI-registration check now asserts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS['*'] contains quorum_prune and isCommandAllowed('quorum_prune','REVIEW') is true, with a negative control (plan_set refused in REVIEW) so the exit-0 is not vacuous. The stale out-of-scope disclaimer comment was removed; config.ts is in the story scope contract. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673: intent explicitly requires asserting hostVerdictEventCount, verdictFileCount, AND `git rev-parse HEAD` all unchanged after the drift-accept refusal (does not advance HEAD). The bound check (refuses a redundant re-submit when the standing quorum drift-accepts) captures beforeEvents/beforeVerdicts (lines 1640-1641) and asserts them unchanged (lines 1670-1671), but never captures or re-checks `git rev-parse HEAD` before/after the refusal -- unlike every other refusal-leaks-no-state check in this same file (e.g. lines 1545/1552, 1740/1745, 1877/1890, 1943/1951) which do assert HEAD is unchanged via beforeHead. One of the three required invariants in this adversarial intent is unverified.
findings.resolvedReason: The drift-accept refusal check now captures git rev-parse HEAD before the refusal and asserts it unchanged afterwards, matching the sibling refusal-leaks-no-state checks. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence reuses happy:1 assertion, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673 (lines 1633-1636): the intent explicitly states storyFilesHash equality is necessary but not sufficient and requires an independent check that commitMainDrift touches zero story-owned file blobs. The bound evidence reuses the exact same storyHashBefore===storyHashAfter assertion already used for CHK-001:happy:1 -- no distinct file-level/diff-based assertion exists anywhere in the suite verifying commitMainDrift only ever touches main-drift.ts; this is proven only by the note ("commitMainDrift helper commits only ... - no story-diff file is touched"), which is a claim about the helpers hardcoded implementation, not an independent runtime check as the intent explicitly demanded.
findings.resolvedReason: New storyOwnedDiffBlobs() helper reads git diff --raw (path, status, destination blob id) between merge-base(main,HEAD) and HEAD filtered by isMaterialExcludedPath. CHK-001:edge:0 now asserts that set is non-empty, deepEqual across the drift, and never contains main-drift.ts, while a whole-tree diff proves the drift really landed main-drift.ts. Shares no code with the storyFilesHash digest. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-003 (quorum_prune) test-coverage gap, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245-2268: no check anywhere in the 12 quorum_prune checks asserts the worktree is clean immediately after a successful `quorum_prune {apply:true}`. quorum-prune.ts:161-169 lifecycleMetadataPaths(kind=quorum-submit) scopes the commit to ONLY process-events.jsonl; writeUniqueBackup() (quorum-prune.ts:125-135, called at :351) writes process-events.jsonl.bak-<timestamp> directly into the tracked story dir and it is never staged/committed by that scoped transaction. .gitignore:32 `*.bak` does not match the `.bak-<timestamp>` suffix, so the backup is left untracked. assertCleanPruneBaseline/assertCleanQuorumBaseline both run an unscoped `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, so the very next quorum_prune or quorum_submit call would refuse on the tools own leftover artifact -- verified live by re-running quorum_prune {apply:true} in a fresh fixture right after a first apply with no intervening commit: it refuses nothing-to-prune only after the backup is manually cleaned. The ONE check that runs prune twice (quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245 never overwrites a previous run backup) masks this because it does its own git add -A + commit between the two applies (lines ~2261-2262), which is not a step a real recovery operator performs. So CHK-003 happy path claim (userSees: the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level / official low-friction recovery) is unverified at the worktree-cleanliness level and is contradicted once you try the very next legitimate action. (Independently corroborates a live concurrent lattice-review-quality RR-003 finding on the same defect, verified here from the test-coverage angle: no verificationEvidence row demonstrates clean-after-apply.)
findings.resolvedReason: Same root cause as F-002 and fixed by the same change: the backup now matches the *.bak ignore rule so a real operator's second recovery call works with no manual git commands. The new twice-apply smoke check has no intervening git add/commit, so it can no longer mask the leftover-artifact failure. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-003 userSees literally documents `lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists the duplicate verdict events...; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits...`, and plan.md CHK-003 specifies the command input as `dryRun` (default true) requiring explicit `apply:true` to mutate. But packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2994-3001 (quorum_prune schema) and packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:34-39 (QuorumPruneArgs) define ONLY an `apply` field — there is no `dryRun` field anywhere in the schema or handler. Empirically verified live against the real repo: `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --storyId=B-3144` (no flags at all, i.e. omitting --dryRun exactly as userSees describes) still prints `mode: dry-run (no mutation)` — it does NOT back up/remove/commit as userSees claims. The `--dryRun` flag is silently swallowed as an unrecognized key (flag-parser.ts has no schema-strictness) and has zero effect on behavior; the only way to actually mutate is the undocumented-in-userSees `--apply` flag. An operator following the story's own documented usage would be misled about how to trigger the recovery.
findings.resolvedReason: quorum_prune now declares a real dryRun boolean in both the catalog schema and QuorumPruneArgs, following the capability_release_backfill convention (default true unless apply=true). --dryRun is honored instead of being silently swallowed, and dryRun:true combined with apply:true is refused before any file read or mutation. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered (same root cause as F-008): because quorum_prune has no `dryRun` schema field, packages/main/src/cli/help-renderer.ts:150-151 dryRunHelpLine() falls through its no-dryRun-field branch, matches /dry-run/i against the tool description text, and prints `Dry-run: always-on. This command only projects guidance and does not execute the side-effect path.` in `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --help` — empirically verified live. This is actively wrong: `apply:true` performs a real mutating side effect (writes a timestamped backup, rewrites the committed process-events.jsonl, and creates a git commit via captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction/commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction in packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:338-366). For a recovery command whose entire safety design (plan.md Risks section) rests on dry-run-by-default + explicit apply, the auto-generated --help text tells operators the opposite of the truth about when it mutates state.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by the same dryRun schema field: help-renderer now derives the default-on branch, so --help prints 'Dry-run: default-on via --dryRun=true ... Default true unless apply=true; passing dryRun:true together with apply:true is refused' instead of the inverted 'Dry-run: always-on. This command only projects guidance and does not execute the side-effect path.' Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-003 userSees (.lattice/story/actives/B-3144/checklist.json) still literally claims `lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists...; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits, and the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level.` Empirically re-verified live against the CURRENT committed code (post f1bcba3885, dist rebuilt): `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --storyId=B-3144` (no --dryRun flag at all, exactly the without-dryRun case userSees describes) and `quorum_prune {"storyId":"B-3144","dryRun":false}` BOTH still print `mode: dry-run (no mutation)` and do NOT back up/remove/commit. In packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:214-221, the mutating apply path is gated SOLELY by explicit `apply:true` (`const apply = args.apply === true;` ... `if (!apply) { ...dryRun:true... }`); the newly-added `dryRun` field (F-008 fix) only participates in the apply+dryRun conflict-refusal check, it never itself flips execution into the apply branch. F-008/F-009 fixed the swallowed-flag and inverted --help wording, but did not correct this specific userSees clause, which still conflates omitting --dryRun with passing --apply=true. Live CLI output (`note: dry-run only — re-run with apply:true...`) does self-correct an attentive operator, so this is not a safety inversion like the original F-009, but the story checklist itself still documents a behavior the current code does not deliver.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 7eb91080fd by making the behavior match the frozen userSees rather than editing the promise. An explicit dryRun:false now executes exactly like apply:true (quorum-prune.ts: apply = args.apply === true || args.dryRun === false), so the flag is no longer a silent no-op. Omitting dryRun still defaults to the safe projection, and apply:true + dryRun:true is still refused, so neither the safety default nor the repo convention (capability_release_backfill) was weakened. New smoke check quorum_prune dryRun:false executes instead of being a silent no-op asserts both directions: omitted = no commit and no backup; explicit false = commit + backup + 6 removed verdicts + clean tree. Smoke 61 to 62 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test exit 0.

findings.desc: doc-behavior-mismatch: F-010 (commit 7eb91080fd) made dryRun:false an executor equal to apply:true, and updated ONLY command-catalog.ts:2997 (the dryRun field describe()) and the function-local comment at quorum-prune.ts:208-218 to say so. Five other prose locations describing the exact same apply/dryRun semantics were left stale, still claiming apply:true is required/the only way to mutate: (1) quorum-prune.ts:20 module comment "dry-run is the default (no mutation without explicit apply:true...)"; (2) quorum-prune.ts:198 user-facing dry-run note "re-run with apply:true to back up, prune, and commit" (never mentions dryRun:false); (3) command-catalog.ts:2994 the TOP-LEVEL tool description shown first in `lattice quorum_prune --help` output — "list (dry-run by default) and, with apply:true, remove duplicate host_verdict events" — inconsistent with the correctly-updated --dryRun flag description three lines below it in the SAME --help output; (4) process-fact-levels.ts:209 rationale "apply:true required to mutate"; (5) command-policy.ts:480 reason "apply:true required to mutate". Verified live: `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --help` prints the stale top-level description at line 1 and the corrected --dryRun description a few lines later, an internal inconsistency visible in the same output block. Before F-010 these five statements were true; the F-010 commit made them false without updating them. No test asserts command-catalog.ts:2994, process-fact-levels.ts:209, or command-policy.ts:480 text, so nothing catches this. Not a broken user promise (apply:true still works) but a genuine half-updated-documentation defect: an operator or auditor reading only the top-level description or the policy/process-fact rationale forms an incorrect mental model of the mutation trigger.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit e306cc7aad. All five stale prose sites now name both executors: quorum-prune.ts module comment (rewritten to state dry-run is the default and execution requires apply:true or the equivalent dryRun:false, with both contradictory pairs refused), quorum-prune.ts dry-run note text, command-catalog.ts top-level description (the first --help line, which had contradicted the corrected flag description in the same output), process-fact-levels.ts rationale, and command-policy.ts reason. A new smoke check 'every quorum_prune apply/dryRun description states both executors' reads the three source files directly and asserts each description mentions dryRun:false and no longer claims apply:true is the only mutation trigger, so this drift cannot silently recur.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:219-226 (F-010 fix): the conflict refusal only catches apply:true && dryRun:true. It does not catch the symmetric conflict apply:false && dryRun:false — verified live: with args={apply:false,dryRun:false}, `const apply = args.apply === true || args.dryRun === false` evaluates to true, so the command silently EXECUTES (backs up, rewrites, commits) even though the caller explicitly passed apply:false. This breaks the code's own stated design philosophy (comment at line ~211-218 and the existing apply:true+dryRun:true refusal): an explicitly conflicting combination should be REFUSED, not silently resolved toward the more dangerous (mutating) outcome. Reachable via both programmatic args and CLI (--apply=false --dryRun=false parses to {apply:false,dryRun:false} per cli/flag-parser.ts coerce()). Fix: extend the refusal check to `(args.apply === true && args.dryRun === true) || (args.apply === false && args.dryRun === false)`, or otherwise treat an explicit apply:false as an unconditional veto regardless of dryRun.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit e306cc7aad. The F-010 fix's resolution apply = args.apply === true || args.dryRun === false made {apply:false, dryRun:false} evaluate to true, so an explicit apply:false silently executed a backup+rewrite+commit — a contradiction resolved toward the MORE dangerous side, violating the same conflict rule stated in the adjacent comment. The symmetric pair now refuses with a message naming both intents, mirroring the existing apply:true + dryRun:true refusal. New smoke check 'quorum_prune refuses the symmetric apply:false + dryRun:false conflict' asserts the refusal makes no commit and no backup, and that apply:false alone still projects.

findings.desc: doc-behavior-mismatch (F-011 recurrence, uncaught by its own regression guard): the e306cc7aad commit that added the apply:false+dryRun:false refusal and fixed 5 F-011 prose sites left three MORE apply/dryRun prose locations stale, two of them directly user-facing in the SAME --help block the F-011 fix targeted. (1) packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2997 dryRun field describe() still says only "passing dryRun:true together with apply:true is refused" -- silent about the apply:false+dryRun:false refusal added in this same commit. (2) packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2998 apply field describe() was never touched by either F-010 or F-011: it still reads "Actually back up, rewrite, and commit; default false = dry-run" with no mention that dryRun:false is an equivalent executor or that apply:false+dryRun:false conflicts. Live-verified via `lattice quorum_prune --help` (built dist in an isolated scratch worktree): the printed --dryRun and --apply argument lines contradict the correctly-updated top-level description printed 3 lines above them in the identical output block -- the exact internal-inconsistency pattern F-011 was filed against, now recurring one level down. (3) packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:42-49 the QuorumPruneArgs.dryRun JSDoc (a sixth prose site, never in F-011's enumerated list of five) still says "dryRun:true together with apply:true is refused rather than silently resolved" with no mention of the F-012 symmetric case. The new regression-guard check added in the same commit (quorum-submit-smoke.ts, check 'every quorum_prune apply/dryRun description states both executors') only reads the catalog top-level description, process-fact-levels.ts, and command-policy.ts -- it never reads the dryRun/apply describe() strings themselves (the actual per-flag help lines shown to operators) nor quorum-prune.ts's own JSDoc, so its stated purpose ("so this drift cannot silently recur") does not hold for the two most operator-visible locations, and did not catch this live gap.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit ed50a2591e. The F-011 guard read only the three block-level descriptions and never the per-flag describe() strings, which are exactly what help-renderer prints per argument — so --help rendered a correct top-level description above a stale --dryRun line and a never-updated --apply line, the same half-updated-docs pattern one level down and inside the guard own blind spot. Both schema describe() strings and the QuorumPruneArgs JSDoc (the sixth prose site, never in F-011 enumerated list) now state both executors (apply:true and the equivalent dryRun:false) and both refusals (apply:true+dryRun:true, apply:false+dryRun:false). The guard now covers all six sites, additionally asserts the two RENDERED --help lines are not stale so the assertion is not source-only, and fails loudly with declaration shape changed if the type declaration moves instead of silently slicing an empty string. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test exit 0.

findings.desc: doc-behavior-mismatch (F-011/F-013 recurrence, still uncaught): F-013 (commit ed50a2591e) claims the regression guard "covers all six sites" (packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2591-2611, the `every quorum_prune apply/dryRun description states both executors` check), but the guard's six-item list (catalog top-level description, catalog dryRun describe(), catalog apply describe(), process-fact rationale, command-policy reason, QuorumPruneArgs JSDoc) omits two sites that were THEMSELVES edited by the earlier F-011 fix commit (e306cc7aad) as part of its own claimed "five stale prose sites": (1) the module header comment in packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:20-32 ("Containment (decision.json preMortems): dry-run is the DEFAULT ... apply:true, or the equivalent dryRun:false ... apply:false with dryRun:false, is REFUSED"), and (2) the runtime-rendered dry-run note in formatPruneResult at packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:208 (`note: dry-run only — re-run with apply:true (or dryRun:false) to back up, prune, and commit.`), which is printed on every default quorum_prune invocation (live-verified: `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --storyId=B-3144` in an isolated scratch worktree built from HEAD prints exactly that note line). Both currently state the contract correctly, but neither is asserted anywhere in quorum-submit-smoke.ts (grep for the note text and for the module-comment content returns zero matches outside the source file itself), so if either drifts back toward the exact half-updated-docs pattern F-011 and F-013 were filed against, no test would catch it — the same failure mode the guard exists to prevent, now in the guard's own inventory a second time. Severity medium: no live incorrect behavior today, but the coverage claim in the F-013 commit message is factually incomplete and the risk class is identical to the two prior findings on this exact guard.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 18e479bd8e, by replacing the method rather than extending the list again. The two flagged sites (quorum-prune.ts module header, and the formatPruneResult runtime dry-run note that prints on every default invocation) are now covered, but more importantly the guard no longer relies on a hand-maintained site list at all: it sweeps the five contract files and asserts that every non-test production line documenting this command apply:true contract also names dryRun:false, matched over a context window because prose wraps across lines, and scoped so sibling commands that legitimately keep the apply-only convention are not swept in. The list itself was the defect - it under-covered twice (F-013, then F-014/F-015), each time after it was believed complete. Discovery immediately found a seventh site a list would have missed again: the conflict refusal message told operators to pass apply:true to actually recover. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/config.ts:362 (CHK-003 in-scope file) is a third quorum_prune apply/dryRun prose site exhibiting the exact half-updated-docs pattern F-011/F-013 target, and unlike the two sites F-014 already flagged (quorum-prune.ts:20-32 module comment and quorum-prune.ts:208 formatPruneResult note, both currently correct), this one is CURRENTLY stale right now: the DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS inline comment reads "dry-run default, apply:true backs up + rewrites + commits" with no mention of the dryRun:false equivalent executor, unchanged since before F-010 introduced dryRun:false as an executor. Neither the F-013 drift guard (which reads only command-catalog.ts, process-fact-levels.ts, command-policy.ts, and the quorum-prune.ts handler - never config.ts) nor any other check in quorum-submit-smoke.ts references this line (grep for the exact phrase and for config.ts source-reading in the smoke file returns zero hits); the guards F-013 fix commit message claims cover the contract are the guards own six-plus-two enumerated sites, not this one, and CHK-003s own verificationEvidence for the config.ts wiring (CHK-003:happy:2) only asserts the behavioral DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS array membership, never the comment text. WHY: this is a live, present-tense documentation defect (not a future-drift risk) in a file the checklist explicitly scopes to CHK-003, in the identical bug class this story spent three fix rounds trying to make un-recurrable, and it currently has zero test coverage from any direction.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 18e479bd8e. packages/main/src/core/config.ts:362 inline DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS comment now reads dry-run default, apply:true or the equivalent dryRun:false backs up + rewrites + commits - it was a genuinely stale instance of the half-updated-docs pattern, distinct from F-014 two sites which were correct but unguarded. config.ts is now inside the guard sweep (it was in CHK-003 files.modify scope but had never been read by any check), and the guard is discovery-based rather than list-based so a new mention anywhere in the five contract files either satisfies the contract or fails the check. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2630 (F-014/F-015 discovery-sweep exclusion regex /args\.apply|args\.dryRun|throw new Error|^\s*\+ '/): the ^\s*\+ ' clause unconditionally skips ANY line that is a multi-line string-concatenation continuation, not just lines that are already covered as part of an already-checked message. quorum-prune.ts already has 6 such continuation lines (e.g. lines 232-233, 243), and 3 of them (232, 233, 243) themselves contain the literal 'apply:true' trigger text but are silently excluded from ever entering the `discovered` array, so they never get the dryRun:false pairing check and do not count toward the discovered.length>=6 floor. Confirmed by replicating the exact loop body against a synthetic new throw-message whose first line does not mention apply:true and whose ONLY apply:true mention sits on a `+ '...'` continuation line paired with no dryRun:false anywhere in the message: discovered.length===0, i.e. a genuinely stale apply:true-only claim added on a continuation line (the file's own dominant style for multi-line throw new Error messages) is completely invisible to the sweep. This defeats the stated purpose of the F-014/F-015 fix ("a new mention anywhere now either satisfies the contract or fails this check; it can no longer be silently missed") for exactly the failure class that has already recurred three times in this story (F-011/F-013/F-014/F-015): a future edit documenting the apply:true contract on a new prose line the guard does not actually check. WHY: the guard's job is specifically to make this class of regression impossible to reintroduce silently; a demonstrable blind spot in its own exclusion regex reopens exactly that risk. Severity: medium (no live incorrect claim exists in the current tree; this is a hardening gap in the regression guard itself, not a currently-shipped functional defect).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit c2e20023e1 by changing the instrument, not patching the regex. The line-oriented sweep unconditionally skipped multi-line string-concatenation continuations, so three real continuation lines carrying apply:true in quorum-prune.ts were never checked, and a synthetic new error message with its only apply:true on a continuation line produced discovered.length===0. The sweep now parses with TypeScript: a concatenated string expression is folded into ONE prose unit, so a claim on any operand is judged together with the whole message, and continuation lines are no longer separately escapable. Executable logic is excluded because it is syntactically neither comment nor string, not because a regex guessed at it. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2622-2642 (DISCOVERY sweep, commit 18e479bd8e, fixing F-014/F-015): the sweep's own claim ("Adding a new mention anywhere now either satisfies the contract or fails this check; it can no longer be silently missed") is falsifiable for two concrete, reproducible patterns a future edit is very likely to use, both giving ZERO signal (not even counted toward discovered.length): (1) fusing new stale prose onto a line that also contains a token matched by the exclusion regex /args\.apply|args\.dryRun|throw new Error|^\s*\+ '/ at line 2630 -- e.g. `if (args.apply) throw new Error('quorum_prune refuses: apply:true required, nothing else needed.')` written as one line -- is dropped from `discovered` entirely, so it never reaches the dryRun:false assertion at line 2636 nor the >=6 floor at line 2639; (2) for the three requireSelfMention files (command-policy.ts, config.ts, process-fact-levels.ts) the self-mention check `line.includes('quorum_prune')` at line 2627 is evaluated on the SAME single line as the apply:true candidate, not over the +/-3-line context window used only for the dryRun:false match (line 2633) -- so a wrapped two-line comment naming quorum_prune on one line and stating a stale apply:true-only claim on the next line is also invisible, which is exactly the multi-line-wrap shape the guard's own comment (line 2631-2632) says it protects against. Verified by extracting the literal candidate/exclusion/window logic (lines 2626,2627,2630,2633,2636) into a standalone script and feeding it synthetic stale lines shaped like both patterns: both yield discovered=[] and failures=[]. A milder third variant: the +/-3-line window is not scoped to one sentence, so two distinct, unrelated apply:true statements placed within 3 lines of each other let a genuinely stale second one borrow the first (correct) one's dryRun:false mention and pass (discovered includes both, failures=[]). None of these are live false negatives against the current 5 files today (real sweep run: discovered.length=12, failures=[], all 12 sites genuinely compliant) -- but they mean the exact failure mode this round exists to close (a new apply:true prose mention silently going unswept, the F-010->F-011->F-013->F-014/F-015 recurrence) can still happen for the two most natural styles of writing a one-line validation-throw or a wrapped two-line comment. WHY: exclusion and self-mention are single-line-granular while only the dryRun:false assertion is window-aware, so the completeness guarantee holds only for lines shaped like the current 12 sites, not for equally plausible future ones.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit c2e20023e1. All three escapes are closed by parsing prose units with TypeScript instead of matching lines. (1) Whole-line exclusion fusing: executable logic is now excluded syntactically (it is neither a comment nor a string literal), so a stale claim cannot hide by sharing a line with args.apply or a continuation prefix. (2) Self-mention line-granularity: scoping and pairing are now deliberately different granularities and documented as such - pairing is strict INSIDE the prose unit so no claim can borrow a neighbour wording, while scoping is wide over surrounding lines because the command name legitimately sits beside the unit (quorum_prune key above a reason string, or trailing comment after the phaseTools entry). Getting these backwards was the reported bug. (3) Window cross-contamination: the pairing assertion no longer reads a line window at all; it reads only the unit text, so a stale statement cannot borrow a neighbour dryRun:false. On (b): the floor was raised from >= 6 to >= 10 against 12 real sites and earned its keep immediately - the first AST pass under-covered by 3 and the floor caught it, which the old >= 6 would have passed silently. On (c): confirmed still loud - readFileSync on a renamed contract file throws ENOENT during check setup. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2650-2661 (proseUnitsOf comment-merge, commit c2e20023e1): the merge that turns contiguous // lines into ONE prose unit is pure line-contiguity, not sentence-scoped, so pairing can still silently borrow a correct dryRun:false from an unrelated sentence in the same merged block -- the exact escape class (3) this commit claims to have closed ("pairing is judged INSIDE the prose unit ... a claim cannot borrow a neighbour wording"), just relocated from the old +-3-line window to the comment-merge boundary. Reproduced with the exact extracted proseUnitsOf/scan logic: a 2-line adjacent // comment ("// First sentence: apply:true executes and dryRun:false is equivalent." followed immediately by "// Second sentence, same paragraph, contiguous line: apply:true is the only trigger here.") merges into ONE unit and produces discovered=[handlers/quorum-prune.ts:2] with failures=[] -- the stale second sentence is silently marked compliant because the merged blob also contains the first, unrelated sentences dryRun:false. This is not hypothetical: running the real sweep against the live packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:13-32 comment shows it is ALREADY a single 20-line merged unit spanning many distinct sentences (containment rationale, backup naming, transaction machinery, floor semantics) that happens to be self-consistent today only because SOME sentence in the block mentions dryRun:false -- any future edit adding a stale apply:true-only sentence anywhere in that block, or any other multi-sentence // block in the swept files, would produce zero failure signal and would not depress the discovered count. WHY: a stale-claim escape inside a merged block is invisible to both the per-site assertion and the >=10 floor (discovered.length is unaffected since the site still counts as one compliant unit), reproducing the un-gameable RED scenario this story exists to prevent.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b22f5b890c. Merging contiguous // lines into one unit only relocated the borrowing escape from the old plus-minus-3-line window to the comment-block boundary, and quorum-prune.ts lines 13-32 is exactly such a multi-sentence block. Comment units are now split back apart by SENTENCE after the contiguity merge, so each claim is judged against the sentence that makes it and cannot borrow a sibling sentence dryRun:false. apply:true and dryRun:false contain no sentence-ending period, so splitting on period-plus-whitespace cannot bisect a claim. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2668-2674 (contractSources, commit c2e20023e1): the discovery sweep still hand-maintains a manually curated FILE list (5 entries) even though the commit message frames its purpose as replacing hand-maintained enumeration with discovery ("A hand-maintained site list is the defect... So DISCOVER the sites instead of listing them"). packages/main/src/handlers/lattice-cli.ts is a CHK-003-declared modify-scope touchpoint for this story (checklist.json CHK-003 files.modify, and the current REVIEW round scope-contract.allowedModify both list it) and already carries quorum_prune-specific prose (lines 529-531: a // comment explaining why quorum_prune is registered via registerBatch alongside createQuorumSubmitHandlers) -- i.e. it is an established, in-scope site for exactly this kind of commentary, not a random unrelated file. It is entirely absent from contractSources, so a future edit adding an apply/dryRun claim there (a very plausible place, since the surrounding comment already narrates quorum_prune-specific behavior) would never enter proseUnitsOf/discovered at all -- zero signal, and the >=10 floor would not move because the site never existed for it. Verified: grep -rln quorum_prune packages/main/src includes handlers/lattice-cli.ts and packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts (also excluded), neither of which appears in the contractSources array. WHY: this reproduces, for FILES rather than LINES, the exact class of bug that already recurred 3 times in this story (F-010/F-011/F-013 stale line, F-014/F-015 stale-list-of-lines) -- a hand-maintained enumeration silently drifts stale as soon as the contract is documented somewhere the list-writer did not anticipate, and the story-declared scope for this very story already names one such place.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b22f5b890c by deriving the list rather than extending it. The swept file set is now read from the story own signed scope-contract.json (allowedModify plus allowedCreate, minus allowedTest), which already enumerates every file this change may touch - including lattice-cli.ts, the CHK-003 touchpoint carrying quorum_prune prose that the hand-written list had missed. A file entering the story scope now enters the sweep automatically and a hand-edited list can no longer drift behind it. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2690-2691 (namedNearby, commit c2e20023e1): for the three requireSelfMention files (command-policy.ts, config.ts, process-fact-levels.ts), self-mention scoping is bounded to sourceLines.slice(line-4, line+3), a ~7-line window. Reproduced with the exact extracted logic: a synthetic command-policy.ts-shaped entry with `quorum_prune: {` on line 2 and a stale `reason: apply:true...` string moved to line 13 (10 lines below the key, still inside one JS object literal spanning the same entry) yields discovered=[] -- the site never enters `discovered` at all, so it contributes neither a failure nor a floor-count decrement; it is completely invisible, the same silently-missed outcome F-016/F-017 already flagged for the old regex sweep. This is lower-likelihood than F-018/F-019 today because all three requireSelfMention files currently write each entry as a single line (verified: every command-policy.ts entry, including quorum_prune itself, is one line; process-fact-levels.ts and config.ts likewise) -- but the guard exists precisely to survive a future editor reformatting one of those entries onto multiple lines, a completely ordinary JS style (and already the dominant style used elsewhere in this same story, e.g. quorum-prune.ts contractSources array and QuorumPruneArgs JSDoc fields), and the widened window described in the commit message ("scoping is wide... answered over the surrounding lines") is not actually wide enough to survive it. WHY: the fix explicitly reframes scoping vs pairing as intentionally different granularities to close F-017, but the chosen scoping granularity (+-3/4 lines) is still a fixed line-count window rather than being anchored to the enclosing syntactic entry (e.g. the object literal or array element containing the prose), so it inherits the same structural fragility as the parts of the guard it replaced.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b22f5b890c. namedNearby no longer uses a fixed line-count window; it resolves the enclosing syntactic entry (property assignment, variable or expression statement) via the TypeScript AST and checks that entry text, falling back to the physical line only for the array-element style (quorum_prune comma trailing comment) which has no per-entry node. Prose therefore stays in range however the entry is formatted, including the multi-line style already used elsewhere in this story code. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2689-2696 (F-019 fix): the swept-file derivation reads only scope-contract.json allowedModify+allowedCreate, but the story genuinely also modified packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts (11 lines, the B-3144 F-001 quorum_prune codex_cli-append exclusion) via an acknowledged-expansion (scope-contract.json acknowledgements[1], paths:[cli-engine.ts]) rather than a formal allowedModify entry. cli-engine.ts already carries quorum_prune-specific prose (the F-001 comment block) but is invisible to the sweep. Reproduced empirically in an isolated worktree: inserting an identical stale apply:true-without-dryRun:false comment next to the existing quorum_prune exclusion in cli-engine.ts leaves the smoke suite fully green (64/64), while the same probe in lattice-cli.ts is correctly caught. This is the exact F-011..F-020 defect class (stale-enumeration of the sweep source) recurring one field deeper: the fix commit claims the scope contract now enumerates every file this change may touch, but scope-contract.ts:252 isAcknowledged()/its own acknowledgements field is part of what the codebase treats as in-scope, and that field is not unioned into sweptFiles. WHY: any future apply/dryRun-contract prose added to cli-engine.ts (a very plausible place, since it already documents quorum_prune mutation-adjacent behavior) ships unguarded while the guard reports full coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 6110491ecb. sweptFiles now unions acknowledgements[].paths alongside allowedModify and allowedCreate, so a file that enters the story real scope through an acknowledged expansion is swept like any other. cli-engine.ts was exactly that case (acknowledged for the F-001 codex_cli exclusion, carrying quorum_prune prose), and the codebase own isAcknowledged() in core/scope-contract.ts already treats acknowledged paths as in scope - this guard and the scope checker were using two different meanings of in this story scope and now use one. Verified by positive probe rather than by absence of failure: planting the comment quorum_prune mutates only with apply:true into cli-engine.ts made the suite fail with cli-engine.ts:1232 documents apply:true without naming dryRun:false as the equivalent executor; the file was then restored via git checkout and rebuilt clean. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: F-020 recurrence: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2748-2761 (namedNearby) does not deliver the guarantee its own comment at lines 2743-2746 states ("Anchor to the enclosing syntactic entry instead ... so however that entry is formatted, prose inside it stays in range"). The walk records the INNERMOST PropertyAssignment/VariableStatement/ExpressionStatement containing the offset as `enclosing`. For a single-line entry like command-policy.ts:480 (`quorum_prune: { ..., reason: "...apply:true..." },`) this happens to work because none of the inner fields individually contain the line-start offset, so `enclosing` stays at the outer `quorum_prune: {...}` assignment whose text includes the command name. But if that same entry is reformatted across multiple lines (e.g. `quorum_prune: {\n  reason: "...apply:true...",\n}`, an entirely ordinary edit for these already-400+-char lines, and the exact scenario F-020 itself was filed to defend against) the innermost enclosing node becomes the `reason: "..."` PropertyAssignment itself, whose own text does NOT include "quorum_prune" (the key lives on the outer, sibling line) — so `enclosing.getText().includes("quorum_prune")` is false, and the physical-line fallback (`sourceLines[line-1].includes("quorum_prune")`) also fails because the key is on a different physical line. `namedNearby` returns false, the site is silently dropped from `discovered` (no failure, no floor decrement), reproducing the exact silent-coverage-hole failure mode (F-013/F-017/F-020) this guard exists to close. Verified empirically: extracted the exact `namedNearby` algorithm into a standalone script against a synthetic multi-line-reformatted command-policy.ts-shaped source; result: `enclosing node text: reason: \x27Official recovery: an explicit apply:true or the equivalent dryRun:false is required to mutate.\x27` and `namedNearby result: false`. WHY: this is a misleading comment (a false, falsifiable guarantee) plus a real maintainability hazard — after 10 iterations (F-011..F-021) explicitly chasing this exact class of silent coverage hole, the current fix still does not survive the single most ordinary future edit (wrapping a long single-line object literal across multiple lines) that its own comment claims to survive.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 687ca32583. namedNearby kept only the INNERMOST enclosing node, so reformatting quorum_prune: { reason: ...apply:true... } across lines made that node the reason assignment itself, whose text lacks the command name because the key is a sibling on another line - both the AST check and the physical-line fallback then failed and the site left the sweep silently. The walk now returns true when ANY ancestor names the command, which is what the comment guarantee however that entry is formatted has to mean, since the quorum_prune key always encloses the reason string it owns. The real defect here was a comment promising protection the code did not deliver, which is worse than no comment. Verified by isolated probe against the exact reformatted shape, running BOTH implementations over the same fixture: innermost-only returns false (reproducing the reported escape) and any-ancestor returns true. Also observed during probing that the guard is two-layered - the hardcoded per-site assertions caught a planted stale reason even while the sweep was blind - so the escape was never the only line of defence. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2748-2772 (namedNearby, F-022 fix commit 687ca32583): the any-ancestor walk stops at the FIRST (outermost) qualifying node (PropertyAssignment/VariableStatement/ExpressionStatement) whose FULL TEXT contains the substring quorum_prune anywhere in its span, preorder from the SourceFile down — not the smallest ancestor that actually names the command near the offset. For every requireSelfMention:true file whose whole command table is ONE top-level statement, that outer statement is the first node visited and its text trivially contains quorum_prune (the entry lives inside it), so namedNearby now returns true for EVERY line in the entire table, including sibling commands the comment two lines above (2679-2682) explicitly says must stay out ("Scope: sibling commands ... legitimately keep the apply-only convention, so only THIS command's prose is swept"). Verified with the current implementation copied verbatim: namedNearby(offset of command-policy.ts:479, the quorum_submit sibling entry inside the same COMMAND_POLICIES object as quorum_prune at :480) === true, and namedNearby(offset of command-policy.ts:155, the unrelated story_resume entry) === true; the pre-fix innermost-only implementation correctly returned false for both. Same structural exposure confirmed for config.ts (DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, one statement from :263) and process-fact-levels.ts (PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS, one array from :46) via the same probe. It does not fail the suite today only because no sibling command's reason/description text in these 3 files currently contains apply:true; the first ordinary future edit that adds such phrasing to an unrelated command in these shared tables will either be force-paired against quorum_prune's dryRun:false convention it has nothing to do with (spurious unrelated failure) or, if it happens to satisfy the pairing, validate nothing about quorum_prune. This is the same comment-promises-more-than-code-delivers pattern this exact guard has been fixed for repeatedly (F-011..F-022), now in the opposite direction (too wide instead of too narrow).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit e7d9a961d3. The F-022 fix over-corrected: any ancestor whose TEXT contains quorum_prune matched the single top-level statement that holds each file entire command table, so namedNearby returned true for every row in that table, including the sibling commands the sweep must leave alone (confirmed at command-policy.ts:479 quorum_submit and :155 story_resume). The walk now matches the entry KEY instead of text containment: a PropertyAssignment whose name is quorum_prune is exactly the entry that owns its own prose, it encloses the reason string however that entry is wrapped, and a sibling keyed quorum_submit never matches whatever the enclosing table contains. Array-element style keeps the physical-line fallback. Verified BEFORE committing with a four-scenario probe running all three implementations over the same fixture (owned reason after cross-line reformat, unrelated sibling story_resume, sibling quorum_submit, array-element style): innermost fails the owned-reason case, anyText fails both sibling cases, keyMatch passes all four. Smoke 64 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test clean.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex (independent second host, run 2026-08-13) reported: quorum_prune can erase a genuine FAILING verdict and turn an invalid round into a passing one. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:275 groups every host_verdict by runId+host/session/key WITHOUT checking decision, required binding fields, material freshness, or storyFilesHash, and line 321 retains the later row. core/host-independence.ts:151 treats a current-material non-PASS as an invalidating fact for that round. If a FAIL row precedes a PASS row with the same identities, default pruning deletes the FAIL and a previously INVALID round becomes valid - the recovery command can launder a failed review. Fix: restrict recovery to the canonical B-bf52 PASS/drift collision shape and fail closed on non-PASS or malformed members.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: quorum_prune now refuses to launder a non-pass duplicate group instead of erasing a genuine FAILING verdict. Verified by dedicated passing regression check 'quorum_prune refuses a non-pass duplicate group instead of laundering the round (F-024)' in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts, confirmed passing in a full 70/70 smoke run.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex reported: unvalidated verdictId permits path traversal during verdict-cache deletion. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:167 joins a committed row raw verdictId into a verdictId.json path with no containment validation. A verdictId such as dot-dot-slash traversal resolves to the repository package.json; after the evidence commit, rmSync deletes it and the command still reports success. Fix: require the canonical verdict-ID shape and verify the resolved path stays directly beneath the story verdict directory.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: verdict-cache deletion path is validated so a verdictId cannot path-traverse outside the story verdict dir. Verified by dedicated passing regression check 'quorum_prune never deletes a verdict cache path outside the story verdict dir (F-025)' in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts, confirmed passing in a full 70/70 smoke run.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex reported: the jsonl rewrite has a data-loss race with normal process-event appenders. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:257 reads the source bytes BEFORE the clean checks and transaction capture, and prune never takes the mandatory append lock used at core/process-events.ts:39. An event appended between the read and the in-place rewrite (line 409) is silently overwritten; worse, when a concurrent append causes commit failure, line 440 restores the earlier snapshot and deletes the concurrent row. Fix: serialize read/validate/backup/rewrite/commit against appenders and bind them to the transaction captured bytes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: quorum_prune holds the shared append lock across the read-then-rewrite of process-events.jsonl, closing the data-loss race with normal process-event appenders. Verified by dedicated passing regression check 'quorum_prune holds the shared append lock across read and rewrite (F-026)' in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts, confirmed passing in a full 70/70 smoke run.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex reported: interruption safety is not atomic and the code own claim is false. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:407 overwrites the canonical JSONL in place, so SIGKILL or power loss mid-write can leave a truncated partial working file and the catch rollback never runs. Git HEAD plus a completed backup usually allow manual recovery, but the claimed atomic behavior is not delivered. Fix: write a same-directory temp file, durable write, atomic rename, while holding the event lock.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the pruned log is installed by atomic rename, not an in-place overwrite, so an interruption cannot leave a partially-written file. Verified by dedicated passing regression check 'quorum_prune installs the pruned log by atomic rename, never an in-place overwrite (F-027)' in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts, confirmed passing in a full 70/70 smoke run.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex reported: the quorum_submit duplicate guard is TOCTOU-racy across concurrent submissions. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:498 performs the committed-event check BEFORE the clean-baseline check and transaction capture. Two reviewer-write invocations can both observe no quorum; if one commits before the other captures its baseline, the second captures the first quorum and successfully appends another identical quorum - recreating exactly the poisoning this story exists to prevent. Fix: a per-story command lock, or re-check duplicates bound to the captured HEAD.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: quorum_submit re-checks the duplicate guard against the captured HEAD, closing the TOCTOU race across concurrent submissions. Verified by dedicated passing regression check 'quorum_submit re-checks the duplicate guard against the captured HEAD (F-028)' in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts, confirmed passing in a full 70/70 smoke run.

findings.desc: HOST-B codex reported: exact-material parity still has a normalization hole. packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:502 compares the RAW event value while the consumer normalizes it at core/host-independence.ts:147. A committed verdict carrying materialDigest with surrounding whitespace counts at the floor, but misses BOTH producer branches: raw equality is false, and the normalized drift test sees current material so it is false too. Re-submission can therefore still poison that run. Fix: compare the normalized material in the same-material branch as well.
